abvigen_published_data_is_unreliable.text:
{
  "entry_id": "abvigen_published_data_is_unreliable",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "Abvigen's published product data for the Red PS Fluorescent Particles-COOH line carries documented errors, including a monoclonal-antibody filing and the product name printed in the Particle Size field, in addition to excitation and emission figures that instrument testing has disproved. Nothing on that page should be treated as load-bearing without independent confirmation.",
  "identifiers": {
    "supplier": "Abvigen Inc",
    "catalogue_product": "AFR-0500-COOH"
  },
  "source": "prior_run:agentic-microscope@abvigen-verification-2026-09-06",
  "grade": "E3",
  "source_ref": "src_prior_abvigen_verification",
  "validity_conditions": "ABOUT A PUBLISHER, NOT ABOUT A BOTTLE, which is the whole reason this one crossed when the measurements beside it did not. 10.3 rule 1 caps a run taken elsewhere at E3 and, worse, a value about another laboratory's bottle needs a same-stock E5 assumption before it means anything here. This claim needs neither: it is about a document, and this store holds that document (src_abvigen_red_ps_cooh_datasheet), so it is checkable rather than inherited. THIS IS WHAT REVERSED TASK 015. The observation on this bench -- green-excited particles visible at 605 -- is equally consistent with `the bottle is not the Abvigen product` and with `the bottle is the Abvigen product and the sheet is wrong`, and a label that says nothing does not separate them either. What separates them is that the page is independently known to be careless, which makes the second explanation far cheaper. Kept as an entry rather than left in a commit message because a reversal whose reason is not on disk gets re-reversed by the next person holding the same data sheet. WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. It does not say every figure on the page is wrong, and it is not a licence to discard a published number because it is inconvenient. The seven entries taken from that sheet remain on disk at E3 about the type; two of them -- the excitation and emission peaks -- are marked disproved, and that marking rests on two independent instrument observations rather than on this entry. This entry lowers how much an unconfirmed figure from that supplier should be trusted; it does not by itself refute any particular one. 10.2.1: TRANSFER, slot KB entry, 10.3 rule 1, capped E3. NO `grade_tag`, following the seven prior_run entries already on disk, all of which carry none -- and that is a gap rather than a convention. 4.3.1 orders within E3 by grade_tag (peer_reviewed -> textbook -> vendor_spec -> preprint) and `prior_run` is not in that enum, so every prior-project item sorts last inside E3 by default rather than by anyone deciding it should. Against this store's own vendor_spec entries that ordering is arguably backwards here: this claim is an instrument verification of a vendor page, and it sorts below the page. Raised with manager-librarian, who owns the enum; not worked around by borrowing a tag that would describe the evidence falsely.",
  "date": "2026-09-19",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

  "schema_version": "0.1",

  "claim": "The label on the particle bottle in use does not state a product identity. The operator examined it on 2026-09-19 and reported that it does not say.",
  "source": "operator_read:kyuhwan_20260919_bottle",
  "grade": "E3",
  "grade_tag": "operator_read",
  "source_ref": "src_operator_read_bottle_20260919",
  "validity_conditions": "AN ABSENCE THAT WAS LOOKED FOR, WHICH IS WHY IT IS AN ENTRY. This entry is what converts the product identification from unconfirmed-and-pending into unconfirmed-and-permanent: before the label was examined, a look at the bottle might have settled it, and now nothing further is scheduled to arrive. Anything that settles it in future has to come from somewhere else. It says nothing about what the particles ARE. It bounds what the bench can tell us, not the sample. IT HAS A SUBJECT NOW. This entry carried none because check 44 rightly refused one -- there was no registry a sample resolved against, and an id was not invented to make it pass. `samples.v0.json` now exists and `subject.kind` takes `sample` (a675c4e), wired to resolve against that table and nothing else. branch_selector_is_pinned_by_integer_not.text:
{
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "date": "2026-09-20",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "seat:librarian",
  "source": "prior_run:agentic-microscope@34a432c",
  "grade": "E3",
  "source_ref": "src_prior_detector_curve_and_branch_20260920",
  "entry_id": "branch_selector_is_pinned_by_integer_not_label",
  "claim": "On the prior project's bench the Lapp branch selector's enum names were false and its integer state was true: the configuration declared the label-to-position mapping inverted, so every label the device reported was the wrong name for the position it was in. The discipline that follows is to select that branch by integer and never by name.",
  "validity_conditions": "WHAT CROSSES IS THE DISCIPLINE, NOT THE LABEL, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE ENTRY. Their `mirror_in`/`mirror_out` strings and their State-to-position mapping are DOWNGRADE under 10.2.1 and are not entered: a label that was wrong there is not evidence here, and copying it would import the defect rather than the lesson. WHAT IT COST THEM: following the labels turned the light off, cost a diagnosis session, and the branch stood BOOKED AS FALSIFIED FOR TWO DAYS before the operator's own mapping showed the mislabelled enum was the fault. The record is worse than that: two further sites had been written by name and would have silently selected the BLOCKING position the moment the labels were corrected. Fixing the names would have broken the working config. Their repair was to convert every functional reference to the integer and to leave the `Label` lines in place only because the GUI needs names to show, with nothing selecting a position by one. WHY THIS MATTERS HERE RATHER THAN THERE: lapp_branch_assignment is open in this store and its own status already says it is settled by ACQUIRING and not by read-back. This entry supplies the reason that sentence is true -- this is the selector whose label and state read back consistently with each other for weeks while the mapping between them was inverted, so every signal a caller would normally trust agreed, and agreed wrongly. IT NARROWS lapp_branch_assignment AND DOES NOT CLOSE IT. The open question is which of widefield_source_a and widefield_source_b is which engine on THIS bench. Nothing here answers that: it is another bench's configuration defect, and 10.3 rule 1 caps it at E3 for exactly that reason. What it changes is what would count as an answer -- a label read back from this stand is not one, and a plan that pins the integer is not exposed to the mapping being wrong. That is a narrowing, and manager-microscope should read it as one. ONE DISCREPANCY IN THE RELAY, recorded rather than smoothed: task 029 quotes the source as saying `State 1 is the Aura position`. The document says State 1 is the measured light-passing position, confirmed 2026-09-04 and re-confirmed 2026-09-06, and separately that the operator gave `mirror_in <-> State 1` on 2026-09-05. Those may be the same position on that bench; the document does not say so, and neither does this entry. NO NUMBERS AND NO `validity`: this is a claim about how a device must be addressed, not a quantity, so a query's condition_range comes back unconstrained rather than satisfied. Slot: A4, device combination. Rule passed: 10.3 rule 2 -- what is taken is sourced to the operator's measurement and the applied configuration, not to the prior repository's prose about them.",
  "identifiers": {
    "selector": "lapp_branch",
    "prior_label": "LappMainBranch1"
  }
}

camera_qe_peak.text:
{
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "date": "2026-09-20",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "seat:librarian",
  "entry_id": "camera_qe_peak",
  "claim": "The Photometrics Kinetix22 has a stated peak quantum efficiency of 0.95, which is the figure its own datasheet gives.",
  "numbers": [
    {
      "name": "quantum_efficiency",
      "value": 0.95,
      "unit": "1",
      "source": "spec:Kinetix22",
      "grade": "E3",
      "precision": "significant_figures",
      "note": "the PEAK, not the QE at any wavelength a question cares about. The datasheet states it as 95 per cent and gives the wavelength dependence only as a graph."
    }
  ],
  "validity_conditions": "A PEAK IS NOT A VALUE AT A WAVELENGTH, and for this camera the difference is large. The borrowed point in camera_qe_at_600nm_from_the_kinetix_graph sits on a curve that falls from its maximum near 550 nm to about 0.42 at 850 nm, so using the peak at a red or near-infrared band overstates the collected signal badly. `validity` carries no wavelength bound because the datasheet attaches none to this figure -- a peak is a maximum over the range, not a claim at a point -- and inventing one would be worse than leaving it unbounded. THIS IS THE FIGURE THAT SURVIVES IF THE CURVE IS EVER REMOVED, which is why it is entered separately from it and at a different grade and source. WHAT WOULD RAISE IT: measuring QE on this camera, which no axis has asked for. Slot: A1. Rules passed: 10.3 rule 1 for the cap, rule 2 for sourcing to the device document. `quantum_efficiency` was unregistered when this entry was written and the registration was raised rather than taken, because quantities.json is manager-librarian's; it landed the same day, defined as electrons per photon and therefore dimensionless, which is why the unit here is `1` and not something new. ITS REGISTRY NOTE RULES ON THE SIBLING, NOT ON THIS ONE: the curve is not an entry and there is no field for one, and the legal shapes are a scalar -- this -- or points a PERSON read, one entry each with the wavelength pinned.",
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "device",
      "id": "camera_red"
    }
  ],
  "source": "spec:Kinetix22",
  "grade": "E3",
  "grade_tag": "vendor_spec",
  "source_ref": "src_photometrics_kinetix22_datasheet_20241021",
  "identifiers": {
    "model": "Kinetix 22"
  }
}

camera_read_noise_dynamicrange.text:
{
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "date": "2026-09-20",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "seat:librarian",
  "entry_id": "camera_read_noise_dynamicrange",
  "claim": "In its DynamicRange mode (16-bit) the Photometrics Kinetix22 has a read noise of 1.6 electrons rms, as specified by the datasheet's CAMERA MODES table. This is the widest dynamic range of the four and the datasheet's default choice when a bright object shares the frame with a dim one.",
  "numbers": [
    {
      "name": "read_noise",
      "value": 1.6,
      "unit": "e",
      "source": "spec:Kinetix22",
      "grade": "E3",
      "precision": "significant_figures",
      "note": "electrons rms, in the DynamicRange mode only. the unit is `e`, registered 2026-09-20 after this seat parked the value in `count` rather than inventing a symbol. The datasheet tabulates 1.6, 2.0, 1.2 and 0.7 across the four modes, a span of 2.9x, so a value quoted without its mode is not a fact about this camera."
    }
  ],
  "validity_conditions": "ONE MODE, AND THE ENTRY CANNOT BE READ FLATLY BECAUSE THERE IS NOTHING FLAT IN IT. The Kinetix22's read noise is a property of the selected camera mode, and the datasheet's CAMERA MODES table gives FOUR: DynamicRange 1.6, Speed 2.0, Sensitivity 1.2, SubElectron 0.7 electrons. They are filed as four entries for the reason the eight polystyrene wavelengths are eight: the datasheet could be wrong about one mode and right about the others, and a mode can be added or withdrawn by a firmware revision. A caller that does not name a mode gets four entries and no single answer, which is the correct refusal. THE TASK ASKED FOR THREE AND THERE ARE FOUR. 029 said three values and `M1/M2/M3`. Three is the mode count of the KINETIX, the 3200-row body, which the same file carries as a separate entry; the installed camera is the KINETIX22, confirmed 2026-08-19 as two bodies on PCIe and matched to the purchase record. The fourth mode is SubElectron at 0.7 electrons -- the lowest of all four, and the one an SNR-limited question would reach for first. Carrying three would have lost exactly the mode A1 most wants. THE UNIT IS `e` AND THE QUANTITY IS ELECTRONS RMS. It was `count` for the first hours of this entry's life, because the registry had no electron unit and 025's lesson is that an entry holding a unit a card would be refused for hands the defect to the first card that cites it. Registering `e`, and registering `read_noise`, were raised rather than taken -- both files are manager-librarian's -- and both landed the same day. `e` and `count` share dimension N and convert by exactly 1; what `e` carries is WHICH thing was counted. The registry's own note warns that ADU must never be given this dimension, because electrons and ADU differ by the camera's gain and sharing N would let the two convert silently. WHAT WOULD RAISE IT ABOVE E3: nothing about reading the sheet, which is still E3. Only measuring the read noise on this camera -- a dark series at the named mode -- makes it E1, and then this entry is superseded rather than edited (rule 8). NOT THE SAME NUMBER AS THE FLAT ONE THE PRIOR PROJECT KEPT. That file sets a single read_noise_e of 1.6 at the top of the block and warns in place that if a third consumer ever reads it flatly and computes, it must be made mode-aware instead. A1 computes SNR and is that third consumer, so this store is mode-aware from its first commit rather than flattened and fixed later. Slot: A1 `snr_floor`. Rules passed: 10.3 rule 1 for the E3 cap, rule 2 for sourcing to the device document.",
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "device",
      "id": "camera_red"
    }
  ],
  "source": "spec:Kinetix22",
  "grade": "E3",
  "grade_tag": "vendor_spec",
  "source_ref": "src_photometrics_kinetix22_datasheet_20241021",
  "identifiers": {
    "model": "Kinetix 22",
    "camera_mode": "DynamicRange",
    "bit_depth_designation": "16-bit"
  }
}

  "claim": "In its SubElectron mode (16-bit, 8x CMS) the Photometrics Kinetix22 has a read noise of 0.7 electrons rms, as specified by the datasheet's CAMERA MODES table. This is the lowest read noise of the four, and the slowest by far.",

      "value": 0.7,
      "unit": "e",
      "source": "spec:Kinetix22",
      "grade": "E3",
      "precision": "significant_figures",
      "note": "electrons rms, in the SubElectron mode only. the unit is `e`, registered 2026-09-20 after this seat parked the value in `count` rather than inventing a symbol. The datasheet tabulates 1.6, 2.0, 1.2 and 0.7 across the four modes, a span of 2.9x, so a value quoted without its mode is not a fact about this camera."
    }
  ],
  "validity_conditions": "ONE MODE, AND THE ENTRY CANNOT BE READ FLATLY BECAUSE THERE IS NOTHING FLAT IN IT. The Kinetix22's read noise is a property of the selected camera mode, and the datasheet's CAMERA MODES table gives FOUR: DynamicRange 1.6, Speed 2.0, Sensitivity 1.2, SubElectron 0.7 electrons. They are filed as four entries for the reason the eight polystyrene wavelengths are eight: the datasheet could be wrong about one mode and right about the others, and a mode can be added or withdrawn by a firmware revision. A caller that does not name a mode gets four entries and no single answer, which is the correct refusal. THE TASK ASKED FOR THREE AND THERE ARE FOUR. 029 said three values and `M1/M2/M3`. Three is the mode count of the KINETIX, the 3200-row body, which the same file carries as a separate entry; the installed camera is the KINETIX22, confirmed 2026-08-19 as two bodies on PCIe and matched to the purchase record. The fourth mode is SubElectron at 0.7 electrons -- the lowest of all four, and the one an SNR-limited question would reach for first. Carrying three would have lost exactly the mode A1 most wants. THE UNIT IS `e` AND THE QUANTITY IS ELECTRONS RMS. It was `count` for the first hours of this entry's life, because the registry had no electron unit and 025's lesson is that an entry holding a unit a card would be refused for hands the defect to the first card that cites it. Registering `e`, and registering `read_noise`, were raised rather than taken -- both files are manager-librarian's -- and both landed the same day. `e` and `count` share dimension N and convert by exactly 1; what `e` carries is WHICH thing was counted. The registry's own note warns that ADU must never be given this dimension, because electrons and ADU differ by the camera's gain and sharing N would let the two convert silently. WHAT WOULD RAISE IT ABOVE E3: nothing about reading the sheet, which is still E3. Only measuring the read noise on this camera -- a dark series at the named mode -- makes it E1, and then this entry is superseded rather than edited (rule 8). NOT THE SAME NUMBER AS THE FLAT ONE THE PRIOR PROJECT KEPT. That file sets a single read_noise_e of 1.6 at the top of the block and warns in place that if a third consumer ever reads it flatly and computes, it must be made mode-aware instead. A1 computes SNR and is that third consumer, so this store is mode-aware from its first commit rather than flattened and fixed later. Slot: A1 `snr_floor`. Rules passed: 10.3 rule 1 for the E3 cap, rule 2 for sourcing to the device document.",

    {
      "kind": "device",
      "id": "camera_red"
    }
  ],

{
  "entry_id": "emission_wheel_filter_positions",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The emission filter wheel holds single-band filters in positions 1 to 4 -- FF01-432/36-32 at 1, FF01-515/30-32 at 2, FF01-595/31-32 at 3, FF01-680/42-32 at 4 -- with a quad-band filter at position 0 whose part number was never supplied. Positions 5 to 8 are blocked by a metal plate.",
  "identifiers": {
    "position_1": "FF01-432/36-32",
    "position_2": "FF01-515/30-32",
    "position_3": "FF01-595/31-32",
    "position_4": "FF01-680/42-32",
    "position_0": "quad-band, part number not recorded",
    "nikon_order_codes": "77015975 / 77015964 / 77015965 / 77015891",
    "vendor": "Semrock BrightLine"
  },
  "source": "prior_run:agentic-microscope@filters-2026-09-06",
  "grade": "E3",
  "source_ref": "src_prior_filter_records",
  "validity_conditions": "THE PAIRING IS INFERRED, NOT CONFIRMED, AND THAT IS THE PRIOR PROJECT'S OWN WARNING carried forward verbatim: `The position<->part pairing is INFERRED from the wheel label naming the EXCITATION line, not stated by the operator. Confirm off the engraving.` So the wheel labels read 405/488/555/647, which are EXCITATION lines, and the parts listed are the emission filters someone matched to them. Nobody read a part number off a filter. USE THIS AT E5, NOT E3. The entry's own grade is E3 because 10.3 rule 1 caps a prior run there, but applying it to the wheel on this bench today stacks two assumptions on top: that the pairing was right when written, and that nothing has been swapped since. 5.8 takes the worst of a chain. The second assumption is lighter than it would be for a consumable -- a filter is a part and stays in its slot unless somebody pulls it, where a bottle gets replaced -- but lighter is not absent, and the bead is precisely why: this store spent a day today on a bottle whose continuity nobody had written down. ONE READING OF THE ENGRAVING SETTLES IT and moves this to `spec:<part>` at E3. That is the same cheap confirmation 10.2's consumables row describes for a lot number: bring the identifier a person can verify by looking, and let them look. WHAT IS NOT HERE: position 0's part number, which was never supplied. The store's EM-Quad-Multiband record lists bands [[432,36],[515,30],[595,31],[680,42]], exactly the four single-bands combined, which is suggestive and is NOT a part number and is not entered as one.",
  "date": "2026-09-19",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

emission_wheel_red_arm_is_position_3.text:
{
  "entry_id": "emission_wheel_red_arm_is_position_3",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "On the prior project's instrument the red particle's emission was strongest through emission wheel position 3, measured by running the same particle through all four single-band positions on 2026-09-06.",
  "identifiers": {
    "part_at_that_position": "FF01-595/31-32",
    "wheel_label": "555",
    "red_arm_position": "3"
  },
  "source": "prior_run:agentic-microscope@filters-2026-09-06",
  "grade": "E3",
  "source_ref": "src_prior_filter_records",
  "validity_conditions": "MEASURED RATHER THAN CHOSEN, and the controls are what make it quantitative. The four positions gave 0.1, 1.6, 362.1 and 62.3 ADU. The first two bands sit blueward of the excitation and cannot carry fluorescence, so they read the floor at about 0.4 percent of the signal -- which is what establishes that the 677-701 band at 17.2 percent is real emission from the red tail of one broad emitter rather than bleed, and that position 3 wins by a real margin rather than a preference. The ADU figures themselves are NOT entered: instrument-specific, DISCARD under 10.2.1, and quoted here only as the reasoning behind the ranking. WHAT IT ESTABLISHES IS A BAND, NOT A PEAK, and the prior project says so itself: `Four bandpasses bracket a band, they do not locate a peak`, which is why it named a TRITC stand-in rather than inventing a number. A6 needs the wavelength actually collected and that is the band of position 3, not a peak inside it. CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY ON THIS BENCH. Today's E2 observation, particles_show_on_the_green_605_path, puts this bottle's emission in the same band on this instrument. Two observations, two instruments, two projects. The prior project's numbers are not borrowed for that -- the agreement is what makes borrowing unnecessary. WHICH WHEEL is not settled by this. emission_wheel_camera_mapping is E5 `operator_recall:` and says the first wheel serves red, `probably`. This entry is about positions WITHIN a wheel and neither confirms nor contradicts it. THE POSITION IS A STRING, NOT A NUMBER, and the schema caught me writing it as one. 5.3's own examples of a nominal designation are `20x` 대물렌즈, `1.5x` 줌 and 필터 위치 `3` -- this exact case. A slot index names WHICH SLOT and asserts no quantity, so it has no uncertainty and no place in numbers[]. I reached for `precision: exact` to express that, which the enum does not have, and the absence is the argument: a value needing `exact` is a value that should not be in numbers[] at all.",
  "date": "2026-09-19",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

filter_cube_mxr00724_is_five_band.text:
{
  "entry_id": "filter_cube_mxr00724_is_five_band",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The cube in the Ti2 filter turret is a Nikon MXR00724, LED-DA/FI/TR/Cy5/Cy7-A, a FIVE-band cube, and it sits in FilterTurret1 position 0. Its emitter passes bands centred at 440, 520.5, 606, 694 and 808.5 nm.",
  "identifiers": {
    "part_number": "MXR00724",
    "product": "LED-DA/FI/TR/Cy5/Cy7-A",
    "turret_position": "0",
    "exciter_bands_nm": "378/50, 474/24, 554.5/21, 635/16, 735/26",
    "dichroic_bands_nm": "432/36, 514.5/31, 595.5/31, 681/40, 808.5/81",
    "emitter_bands_nm": "440/40, 520.5/21, 606/34, 694/34, 808.5/81"
  },
  "source": "prior_run:agentic-microscope@filters-2026-09-06",
  "grade": "E3",
  "source_ref": "src_prior_filter_records",
  "validity_conditions": "FIVE BANDS, AND THE LABEL SAYS THREE. The turret's metadata label reads DA/FI/TR, a three-band set, across all 2312 of the prior project's metadata records -- while 764 frames were shot on 647-Cy5, which a three-band cube passes almost nothing of. The prior project resolved it on 2026-08-10 by reading NIS-Elements Device Manager > Filter Block Settings: the physical part is MXR00724, five bands. A label disagreeing with the part in the slot, discovered by counting frames that should not have worked. THE POSITION IS 0 AND THE SOFTWARE LABEL SAYS 1. The MicroManager label `1-MXR00724 -Empty` reads as position 1 and is wrong twice over -- the turret numbers from 0, and `Empty` was a display artifact. Corrected 2026-09-09 against three independent records including a contrast measurement: state 0 gave 1.00x against 5.16/5.15/5.13x for states 1/2/3, so 0 holds the cube and the rest are empty slots. Setting the turret to 1 inserts an EMPTY slot, which on the confocal path is the difference between blocked and clear. THE EXCITER AND EMITTER ARE SEPARATELY SWAPPABLE. The prior project's note corrects an earlier assumption that a cube is one monolithic block: exciter and emitter are individual units in the cube frame. So the part number identifies a set that was shipped together, not a guarantee that all three pieces are still the ones listed. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE BEAD. The exciter's third band is 554.5/21, i.e. 544-565 nm, and the emitter's third is 606/34, i.e. 589-623 nm. Those are the 555 and 605 the person reported reading -- so the operator's two numbers are this cube's TRITC window pair, which is a more specific account of where they came from than anything this store had. And because the emitter also passes 694/34, a particle emitting in the red is not excluded by this cube; the band is selected downstream in the wheel. E3 AND STILL CARRYING A CONTINUITY ASSUMPTION, like everything else from that repository: it was verified there, not here.",
  "date": "2026-09-19",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

      "unit": "nm"
    }
  },
  "identifiers": {
    "part_number": "FF01-432/36-32",
    "vendor": "Semrock",
    "designation": "432/36"
  },
  "source": "spec:FF01-432/36-32",
  "grade": "E3",
  "grade_tag": "vendor_spec",
  "source_ref": "src_prior_filter_records",
  "validity_conditions": "A VENDOR SPECIFICATION ABOUT A PART, WHICH IS WHY IT IS NOT E5. This does not come through the prior repository even though that is where the part number was found: the passband is Semrock's published specification of FF01-432/36-32, and a part number is a type. Whether this part is in this laboratory's wheel is a SEPARATE claim at E5 (emission_wheel_filter_positions); whether it is in position 3 is another (emission_wheel_red_arm_is_position_3). Keeping them apart is what lets the band arrive at E3 the moment somebody confirms the part off the engraving, instead of the whole chain being dragged to E5. NOMINAL PASSBAND, NOT A MEASURED CURVE. 414.0-450.0 nm is centre plus or minus half the FWHM. A real filter's edges are steeper than that and its blocking is wavelength dependent, so this is a triage figure: adequate for deciding which band collects a dye, not for a blocking calculation. The vendor publishes measured curves and none has been obtained. `validity` pins the passband so a query at another wavelength returns `disjoint` rather than a value. THE SOURCE NAMES THE PART EXACTLY, AS OF a675c4e. It read `spec:FF01-432-36-32` for part of 2026-09-19 because common.schema.json's source pattern had no solidus in its character class -- which excluded the canonical form of every bandpass filter in optics, since they are all designated centre/width. manager-librarian added it. The slug is reverted rather than left: a source token that does not match the part it names reads fine until somebody greps for it. `identifiers.part_number` keeps the designation too, which is where an exact designation belongs regardless.",
  "date": "2026-09-19",
  "supersedes": null,

  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

host_clock_is_not_the_experiment_clock.text:
{
  "entry_id": "host_clock_is_not_the_experiment_clock",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The host clock and MicroManager's frame timestamp series are separate clocks. Mapping host timestamps onto the frame series after the fact is a correlation between two clocks, not a synchronisation of them.",
  "source": "prior_run:agentic-microscope@safety-2026-09-03",
  "grade": "E3",
  "source_ref": "src_prior_safety_memo",
  "validity_conditions": "TWO CLOCKS, AND THE JOIN IS AN INFERENCE. Anything stamped by the host -- a stage move, a trigger, an operator action -- sits on a different timebase from the frames, and aligning them afterwards produces an association whose error nobody has measured. It is not that the offset is large; it is that it is unquantified, so a latency derived across the boundary inherits an unknown. THIS IS THE FACT, NOT THE RULE THAT FOLLOWS FROM IT. Whether the orchestrator may cross that boundary, and what it must record when it does, is a decision for the clock design and not something this entry settles. 10.2.1: TRANSFER. Row: 10.2's hardware-control-path row, whose prerequisite -- the four device-interface functions -- is met, and whose own rule says it does not wait for `envelope/` because wrapping a control path needs no safety limit. Slot: KB entry, named in the 2026-09-18 amendment. Rule: 10.3 rule 1, capped E3. Confirming it on this instrument promotes it to E1 and supersedes this entry.",
  "date": "2026-09-20",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

{
  "entry_id": "lab_ambient_temperature",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The laboratory's ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius, read off a thermometer by the operator. It is a reading and not a setpoint, and it is the room's rather than the sample's -- which is what makes it an operator reading at E3 and not a calibration at E2.",
  "numbers": [
    {
      "name": "ambient_temperature",
      "value": 293,
      "unit": "K",
      "source": "operator_read:kyuhwan_20260917",
      "grade": "E3",
      "precision": "significant_figures",
      "note": "the reading was reported as 20 degrees Celsius. The store carries kelvin because the unit registry is multiplicative -- si_factor and a dimension vector cannot express an offset unit, so Celsius cannot enter it at all. 293 K rather than 293.15 K: the exact conversion would claim five figures from a reading given to the nearest degree, and the 0.15 K it drops is far inside the resolution of the reading."
    }
  ],
  "validity_conditions": "The room as of 2026-09-17, operator read off a thermometer. CORRECTED 2026-09-19: this entry used to reason that the value could not be a setpoint because nothing actuates the temperature. That premise was false and the conclusion was right. The room IS held, by continuous air conditioning; what is not actuated is the SAMPLE, and the entry had collapsed the two. The grade never rested on that argument: 20 C is a value someone READ, which 12 grades differently from a setpoint, and a room value applied to the sample is not a measurement of the sample. A right answer standing on a wrong reason is the thing that rots, and as written the sentence asserted that this room is uncontrolled. The controlled room does not shrink the sample question, it ISOLATES it: with the room held, whatever still moves at the sample is local -- illumination, a contacting objective, the stage -- and those have their own open gap. Do not read 'the room is controlled' as 'temperature is handled'. WHERE the thermometer sits is now stated rather than inferred (no_thermometer_at_the_sample): it reads the room, and how far that is from the sample and how well the two track are both unknown. A plan needing the viscosity or the thermal energy AT THE SAMPLE stands on that gap rather than on this entry. Water's viscosity moves by roughly two percent per kelvin, so in explore mode a drift of about a kelvin does not move a decade and can be ignored, while in confirm mode it cannot. The date the reading was taken is not recorded either -- what is dated 2026-09-17 is the operator's statement that it is a reading.",
  "source": "operator_read:kyuhwan_20260917",
  "grade_tag": "operator_read",
  "subject": [
    {

      "id": "ambient_temperature"
    },
    {
      "kind": "quantity",
      "id": "temperature"
    }
  ],

light_engine_line_intensity_is_per_mille.text:
{
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "grade": "E3",
  "source": "prior_run:agentic-microscope@34a432c",
  "source_ref": "src_prior_mm_device_reported_20260903",
  "date": "2026-09-20",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "seat:librarian",
  "entry_id": "light_engine_line_intensity_is_per_mille",
  "claim": "On both Lumencor engines each light line is exposed as two MMCore properties, `<NAME>` taking 0 or 1 and `<NAME>_Intensity` taking 0 to 1000. The intensity scale is per-mille, not per cent: an operator's 10 per cent is 100, and writing 10 sets one per cent.",
  "validity_conditions": "THIS IS THE RANGE THE REQUEST ASKED FOR AND IT IS NONE OF THE THREE IT OFFERED. Not 0-100, not 0-1, not 0-255: `intensity_unit: \"per-mille (0-1000)\"` appears in the `device_reported:` block of each engine, recorded as read live over MMCore on 2026-09-03. SO THE OPERATOR'S 10 PER CENT RESOLVES TO 100. The factor-of-ten error is not hypothetical there: the source records 5 per cent being written as 50, and warns in the same file that typing 5 gives 0.5 per cent. LINES ARE NAMED, NOT NUMERIC. The Spectra III reports VIOLET, BLUE, CYAN, TEAL, GREEN, YELLOW, RED, NIR; the Aura III reports UV, CYAN, GREEN, RED, NIR. So the property is per LINE and there is no device-level intensity: a plan must name which line it is driving. THE CENTRE WAVELENGTHS OF THOSE LINES DID NOT CROSS. The prior file carries two lists of numeric wavelengths and says twice that they were read from NIS-Elements diagram icons and that the device contradicts them. A line NAME is a nominal designation and a string (5.3); a centre wavelength is a measurement, and that one is not made here. A RANGE IS NOT A LIMIT. 0 to 1000 is what the adapter accepts. What may be commanded on this instrument is envelope/safety.json's and a person's, and 10.3 rule 4 keeps limits out of here entirely. WHAT WOULD RAISE IT: getDevicePropertyNames() and getPropertyLowerLimit/UpperLimit on this stand. Slot: a KB entry and the device registry's control-channel columns. Rule passed: 10.3 rule 1.",
  "identifiers": {
    "vendor": "Lumencor",
    "intensity_property_suffix": "_Intensity"
  }
}

  "claim": "Both Lumencor engines carry a master property `State`, taking 0 or 1, which gates the whole device. With State at 0 no light leaves the engine however a line and its intensity are set, and nothing reports an error or reads back wrongly.",
  "validity_conditions": "THREE PROPERTIES, NOT TWO, AND THE THIRD FAILS SILENTLY. Setting `<NAME> = 1` and `<NAME>_Intensity = 50` is not enough; with the master `State` at 0 the camera returns a frame indistinguishable from a dark frame. There is no exception, and both the line property and the intensity property read back exactly as written, so every signal a caller would normally trust says the light is on. FILED SEPARATELY FROM THE PER-MILLE SCALE UNDER RULE 1: the scale could be right and the master absent, or the reverse, and a stand could be reconfigured to change one without the other. WHAT IT COST THERE, kept as the reason this is worth an entry rather than a note: a run that set only the two line properties produced a field whose median was BELOW the dark frame and a ratio computed almost entirely on the camera's own hot pixels, and it looked like a result. The guard the prior project adopted -- after enabling light, snap through the widest filter and require the median to rise above the dark frame, else refuse -- is a PREFLIGHT SHAPE and belongs to O1 if this system wants it; it is named here and not entered as a rule, because a check is designed and not transferred (10.2.1). COMPOUNDING IT: on that configuration `Core.Shutter` is `LightEngine`, so autoshutter never opens the Aura, and autoshutter is off during a measurement by their own policy. Nothing else opens the engine for you. WHAT WOULD RAISE IT: getDevicePropertyNames() on this stand, plus one acquisition with State at 0 and a line at full to confirm the frame is dark. Slot: a KB entry and the device registry's control-channel columns. Rule passed: 10.3 rule 1.",
  "identifiers": {
    "vendor": "Lumencor",
    "master_property": "State"
  }
}

mm_label_zdrive_is_the_focus_axis.text:
{
  "entry_id": "mm_label_zdrive_is_the_focus_axis",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "On the prior project's configuration the focus axis is the MMCore device label `ZDrive`, moved with setPosition and read with getPosition. Its position is the focus coordinate on this stand.",
  "validity_conditions": "THE LABEL WAS READ FROM CODE POSITIONS AND NOT FROM THE RELAY, which is the whole point of entering it here. It reached this seat as a quotation manager-microscope flagged as unverified -- `ZDrive` in a 28-device list -- and a relayed label is exactly what 10.3 rule 3 keeps out. Verified independently in machine-readable positions: the named constant `Z_DEVICE = \"ZDrive\"`, the set `COLLISION_DEVICES = frozenset({\"Nosepiece\", \"ZDrive\", \"PFSOffset\"})` in three files, `core.getPosition(\"ZDrive\")` at four call sites, and two tests asserting the name. The relay was right and that is not why it is entered. The same discipline caught the opposite case under 028: a docstring named the light engines `SpectraIII`/`AuraIII` while every call site wrote `LightEngine` and `Aura`. THE MM LABEL IS NOT THE REGISTRY ID. Every element on `stand_ti2e` is named in this store's own snake_case -- `nosepiece` for `Nosepiece`, `motor_stage` for `XYStage`, `lapp_branch` for `LappMainBranch1` -- so the element row added with this entry is `z_drive` and the MM label lives here, in `identifiers.mm_label`, the way 028 filed the camera and the engines. Task 035 asked for the MM label in the row's `id`; the table's own convention says otherwise and the convention wins, because an id that is sometimes a registry name and sometimes a device label is not an id. WHAT IT DRIVES IS NOT ENTERED. The document calls the motion `stage motion` in one place and gives `SAMPLE_Z_WINDOW_UM` as `where the sample sits in ZDrive coordinates`, which does not settle whether the objective or the sample carriage moves. On an inverted stand that distinction decides which way a collision closes, so it is left unclaimed rather than inferred. IT CORROBORATES A CLAIM THIS STORE ALREADY HOLDS AT E3. z_retract_direction_is_measured says smaller Z is retracted; the prior document carries `Z_RETRACT_DIRECTION = -1`, measured by the same operator on 2026-09-05, and records that the configurations have said `FocusDirection,ZDrive,1` since 2026-09-06. Two records of one measurement, agreeing. The grade does not rise -- it is the same operator and the same instrument, not a second measurement -- and the store's entry does not need this one. WHAT WOULD RAISE IT: getLoadedDevices() on this stand. Slot: a KB entry and the device registry's stand_ti2e elements. Rule passed: 10.3 rule 1 for the E3 cap, and the label comes from the configuration it was read in.",
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "device",
      "id": "stand_ti2e"
    }
  ],

  "grade": "E3",

A state device answers getState and getStateLabel; there is no `Position` property to compare against getDevicePropertyNames(), which is what the request assumed. A plan naming one will not find it. THE LABEL IS THE LAB'S OWN STRING AND CARRIES THE OBJECTIVE, so it is also how the prior project recovered which objective is in the path. That makes it a nominal designation and a string (5.3), never a number: the prior project's `20.078x` is the case that rule exists for -- a nominal magnification wearing a value back-calculated from a calibration -- and a magnification must not be parsed back out of this label into a number here. THE LABEL SET IS NOT ENTERED. Which position carries which objective is falsified by one person turning the turret, and nosepiece_objective_assignment already says position-to-lens is the one claim on this device a single swap falsifies. What crosses is the INTERFACE, which a swap does not touch. NOT A SAFETY CLAIM. The prior module marks this device as one of three where a move can collide and records that rotating the turret does not retract Z. That is device behaviour and it is named here so nobody reads its absence as its absence -- but it is not entered as a limit, and 10.3 rule 4 keeps limits out: a person writes those after confirming physically. WHAT WOULD RAISE IT: getLoadedDevices() and getDeviceType() on this stand. Slot: a KB entry and the device registry's nosepiece row. Rule passed: 10.3 rule 1.",
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "device",
      "id": "nosepiece"
    }
  ],
  "identifiers": {
    "mm_label": "Nosepiece",
    "parent_stand": "Ti2-E"
  }
}

nosepiece_write_runs_no_escape.text:
{
  "entry_id": "nosepiece_write_runs_no_escape",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The stand runs no objective escape when the nosepiece is rotated by a Micro-Manager write: Z does not move, so whatever height the outgoing objective was at is where the incoming one arrives. Rotating at the stand or in NIS does run the Ti2's own escape; the software path does not.",
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "device",
      "id": "nosepiece"
    },
    {
      "kind": "device",
      "id": "stand_ti2e"
    }
  ],
  "source": "prior_run:agentic-microscope@safety-2026-09-03",
  "grade": "E3",
  "source_ref": "src_prior_safety_memo",
  "validity_conditions": "Ruled TRANSFER under 10.2.1 and passed 10.3 rule 1, so it caps at E3 -- a run taken in another project is not a run taken here. 10.2's hardware-control-path row is open and says in its own rule that it does not wait for envelope/, because wrapping a control path needs no safety limit. Slot: O1 preflight, which is the consumer that has to know a write does less than it appears to, with A4 second. Measured in the prior project by rotating between two objectives and reading the Z drive before and after: it moved by zero. The clearance that absorbs the difference is a property of whichever objective is arriving, and this store already holds those working distances per part number. No limit crosses with this: what is transferred is that the escape does not run, not how far anything may travel.",
  "date": "2026-09-19",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

npcd_analogue_and_digital_commands_are_s.text:
{
  "entry_id": "npcd_analogue_and_digital_commands_are_summed",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The piezo controller takes its commanded position from the analogue input, from digital commands from the host, or from both at once, and when both are enabled the two commands are summed.",
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "device",
      "id": "piezo_stage"
    }
  ],
  "source": "spec:nanobench_6000_user_manual_v1_0_19_s1_2",
  "grade": "E3",
  "grade_tag": "vendor_spec",
  "source_ref": "src_nanobench_6000_user_manual",
  "validity_conditions": "Vendor specification, read from the manual itself (10.3 rule 2); E3 vendor_spec. Slot: the device wrapper and O1 preflight -- with the analogue input enabled, a digital position command is not the position the stage goes to, so the analogue-command setting has to be known before a digital command means what it says. The microscope seat reports that input as disabled on all three channels today; that report is a separate item this seat has not yet been able to check. The same manual section warns that the controller gives only limited protection against configurations that would damage a connected stage. Falsified by a stage that, with both inputs enabled, follows the digital command alone. Delivered as item `prior_analogue_digital_sum` of microscope_agent/findings/microscope-20260924-2-20260924.json at a0fda99 (card 043); the source was opened and its sha256 recorded before this was ruled.",

}

{
  "entry_id": "objective_mrd77400",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "Nikon CFI Apo Lambda S 40XC WI, part number MRD77400: a water-immersion 40x objective of numerical aperture 1.25 with a correction collar, specified for coverglass from 150 to 190 micrometres. Its working distance is quoted as a range, 0.16 to 0.2 mm, because it depends on where the correction collar is set.",
  "numbers": [
    {
      "name": "na",
      "value": 1.25,
      "unit": "1",
      "source": "spec:MRD77400",
      "grade": "E3",
      "precision": "significant_figures"
    },
    {
      "name": "working_distance_min",
      "value": 0.16,
      "unit": "mm",
      "source": "spec:MRD77400",
      "grade": "E3",
      "precision": "significant_figures",
      "note": "the quoted range is carried as its two ends; compressing a range into one value would stop it being a quotation"
    },
    {
      "name": "working_distance_max",
      "value": 0.2,
      "unit": "mm",
      "source": "spec:MRD77400",
      "grade": "E3",
      "precision": "significant_figures"
    }
  ],
  "validity_conditions": "Catalog specification for this part number, capped at E3 because a published specification is not a measurement taken here. The working distance is collar-dependent, and the collar setting is determined once the coverglass thickness is fixed -- so at the 170 micrometres this laboratory uses (coverslip_thickness_in_use) the working distance is a single value rather than a range. The catalog does not publish that value, and the librarian does not interpolate within a quoted range, so it is recorded as a condition_mismatch gap rather than derived. This is the one lens on this nosepiece with a real correction collar. THIS LENS DOES NOT ANSWER TO `working_distance`, AND A PREFLIGHT KEYED ON THAT NAME GETS NOTHING FOR IT. Run against the store: `working_distance` returns five entries, the other five objectives; this one carries `working_distance_min` and `working_distance_max` instead. So a focus ceiling written as `look up working_distance for the lens in use` succeeds for five lenses and comes back EMPTY for this one -- not with a range to think about, with nothing. That is the worse failure of the two, because a range is visible and an absence looks like a lookup that has not run. THE SAFE PATH IS THE PART NUMBER. Task 009 made `identifiers.part_number` addressable, and it works: a query for MRD77400 returns this entry, whose numbers a caller then reads -- getting the interval, and seeing that it is one. A preflight resolving by part number cannot silently miss a lens; one resolving by quantity name already does. WHICH END BINDS IS NOT THE STORE'S TO SAY, and the store can still say which end is conservative: at any collar setting the true working distance is at least the minimum, so a ceiling at 0.16 mm is never passed before focus and a ceiling at 0.2 mm can be. That is geometry, not policy; the choice belongs to the person who writes envelope/safety.json (4.3.2, 10.3 rule 4).",
  "validity": {
    "coverslip_um": {
      "min": 150,
      "max": 190,
      "unit": "um"
    }
  },
  "identifiers": {
    "part_number": "MRD77400",
    "product": "CFI Apo Lambda S 40XC WI",
    "nominal_magnification": "40x",
    "immersion": "water"
  },
  "source": "spec:MRD77400",
  "subject": [
    {

    }
  ],
  "grade": "E3",
  "grade_tag": "vendor_spec",

}

particle_suspension_a_identity.text:
{
  "entry_id": "particle_suspension_a_identity",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The particle suspension in use on this bench, instance particle_suspension_a, is the Abvigen product AFR-0500-COOH. This is the person's ruling of 2026-09-19 from evidence on record, not a reading of the container.",
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "sample",
      "id": "particle_suspension_a"
    }
  ],
  "identifiers": {
    "instance": "particle_suspension_a",
    "catalogue_product": "AFR-0500-COOH",
    "supplier": "Abvigen Inc",
    "what_it_joins": "the instance in kb/staging/samples.v0.json to the type facts filed as tracer_particle_material_and_shape, tracer_particle_density, tracer_stock_concentration, tracer_storage_conditions, tracer_number_density_from_diameter, tracer_emission_peak and tracer_excitation_peak"
  },
  "source": "assumed:person_ruling_20260919",
  "grade": "E5",
  "grade_tag": "person_ruling",
  "source_ref": "src_person_ruling_20260919",
  "valid_until": {
    "date": "2036-09-19",
    "event": "the bottle now in use is replaced, emptied, or decanted into another container. The EVENT is the one that matters and the date is only an outer bound: this claim is about one physical container, and the day a different bottle is on the bench it asserts nothing about it. Note that reading a label does NOT end this claim -- it either raises it to E3 or refutes it, and both of those are entries, not expiries."
  },
  "validity_conditions": "THE JOINING CLAIM, AND IT IS AN ENTRY BECAUSE A STAGING TABLE CANNOT CARRY A GRADE ANYTHING CHECKS. Architecture's instance/type split (6eaee1b) puts three things in three places: the bottle is an INSTANCE and lives in the sample table, AFR-0500-COOH is a TYPE and its facts are ordinary entries at E3, and the claim joining them carries its own grade. This is that claim. It was written into kb/staging/samples.v0.json first, where check 43 does not reach, kb_index.py does not index, and -- decisively -- check 54 cannot resolve it: a `kb:` basis resolves to an entry, so a card applying a type fact to this bench had no citable link and inherited E3 by default, which is the exact over-claim 017 forbade. WHAT EVERYTHING ELSE INHERITS FROM IT. 5.8 gives a chain the worst precision and grade of its inputs, so every type-level fact reaching this bottle passes through E5 here: the material and shape, the density, the stock concentration, the storage range, the number-density relation, and through the material, the eight polystyrene refractive indices. A caller applying any of them to the bench cites this entry as well and takes E5, not the E3 those entries carry about the type. WHAT DOES NOT PASS THROUGH IT. A measurement made ON the instance does not, and that is the whole point of the split rather than a technicality. tracer_diameter_measured is E2 about this bottle; particles_show_on_the_green_605_path is E2 about this bottle; bottle_label_states_no_product is E3 about this bottle. None of the three is weakened by this entry, and if the identification is ever overturned all three stay true while every type fact above stops applying. WHY E5 AND NOT E3. The person did not read it off the container -- bottle_label_states_no_product records that the label was examined and does not state a product identity, which is what makes the doubt permanent rather than pending. It is not a recollection either. It is an inference, and the inference is an asymmetry rather than a measurement: the observation on this bench (green excitation, visible at 605) is equally consistent with `this is not the Abvigen product` and with `this is the Abvigen product and the published spectra are wrong`, and a silent label separates them not at all. What separates them is abvigen_published_data_is_unreliable -- the supplier's page carries two errors unrelated to spectra, a monoclonal-antibody filing and the product name printed in the Particle Size field -- which makes the second explanation far the cheaper one. Cheaper is not proven, and E5 is the grade that says so. WHAT WOULD MOVE IT TO E3. A label, an invoice, or a lot number that names the product, read by a person: any of those is `operator_read:` at E3 and lifts every type fact with it. The lot number is the cheapest and the prior project's own record says `lot: null -- not on the product page, read it off the tube`, which nobody has done. THIS WAS RULED THE OTHER WAY EARLIER THE SAME DAY. Task 015 ruled the product wrong and was executed (8646426); the person reversed it (ed373e0, 017) once the prior project's records were opened. Kept in this entry rather than only in the task file because a caller meeting this claim at E5 will want to know the doubt has been resolved once already, and in which direction. Anyone re-deriving the identification from the label alone will reach 015 again.",
  "date": "2026-09-19",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

pixeltype_misreports_bit_depth.text:

  "entry_id": "pixeltype_misreports_bit_depth",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "MicroManager's PixelType property reports 12bit while the data delivered is 16-bit, so trusting the property scales every count by a factor of sixteen.",
  "source": "prior_run:agentic-microscope@safety-2026-09-03",
  "grade": "E3",
  "source_ref": "src_prior_safety_memo",
  "validity_conditions": "A READ-BACK THAT IS WRONG, WHICH IS THE WORST KIND: it answers, so nothing errors. The prior project's evidence was a single 512x512 frame holding 12,441 distinct values with a modal spacing of 1 LSB and a maximum of 34,917 -- and 34,917 cannot occur in 12 bits, whose ceiling is 4,095, so the maximum alone settles it. Those counts are that project's measurement of their frame and are not entered as numbers here; what transfers is that the property lies. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND SCALING. A bit depth is read to decide saturation, and a sixteenfold error in the ceiling means a frame can be called safe at 85 per cent of a ceiling that is actually sixteen times higher, or clipped without anything noticing. 10.2.1: TRANSFER. Row: 10.2's hardware-control-path row, whose prerequisite -- the four device-interface functions -- is met, and whose own rule says it does not wait for `envelope/` because wrapping a control path needs no safety limit. Slot: KB entry, named in the 2026-09-18 amendment. Rule: 10.3 rule 1, capped E3. Confirming it on this instrument promotes it to E1 and supersedes this entry.",
  "date": "2026-09-20",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": ["kinetix_red_adapter_properties_as_reported_20260924"],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan",
  "identifiers": {
    "property": "PixelType",
    "reported": "12bit",
    "actual": "16-bit"
  }
}

  "entry_id": "red_path_605_is_the_ff01_595_31_filter",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "What this bench calls the 605 path or the 605 band is the FF01-595/31-32 single-band emission filter, not a separate filter designated 605. The two names are one optical path; 605 is a local name and 595/31 is the designation.",
  "validity_conditions": "AN IDENTIFICATION, NOT A MEASUREMENT, AND IT LICENSES NOTHING ABOUT A BAND. It says two names refer to one filter. It does NOT say the path collects at 605 nm: the designated centre is 595 with a 31 nm width, which is filter_ff01_595_31_32_passband at E3 vendor_spec, and 605 sits inside that passband at 579.5 to 610.5 nm near the red edge. No numeric condition applies here, so a query's condition_range comes back unconstrained rather than satisfied. WHY IT IS A SEPARATE FILE FROM THE FLUORESCENCE OBSERVATION. particles_show_on_the_green_605_path records that the particles in the bottle are visible through this band; this records which filter the band is. Each can be refuted without the other -- someone could open the wheel and find a different filter in that position while the particles still fluoresced, or the filter could be confirmed while the observation turns out to have been on another sample. Rule 1 makes that two files. THE GRADE IS E5 BECAUSE NOBODY LOOKED. The person was asked directly where the number 605 came from, with three options offered -- read off the filter wheel, a nickname for the 595/31 filter, or stated from memory -- and chose the nickname. That is a statement about what the bench calls a path, made from memory; it is not a reading at the instrument, and 5.3 does not let the two take the same grade. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: opening the emission wheel and reading the designation on the filter in the red position, which would be `operator_read:` at E3. That is also what would settle WHICH POSITION carries it, which this entry does not claim. NO DEVICE SUBJECT, DELIBERATELY. The obvious one is filter_wheel_em1, and emission_wheel_camera_mapping puts that wheel on the red camera at E5 with the word `probably`. Naming the device here would carry that uncertainty into this entry as though it were settled, which is the laundering this store keeps removing. The subject is the quantity the identification bears on. THE REFRACTIVE-INDEX ENTRIES DO NOT REST ON THIS. water_refractive_index_595nm_293k, water_refractive_index_605nm_293k and the two air entries each stand on a printed grid point in their own source, and each would be exactly as true if this identification were overturned tomorrow. room_temperature_hold_band.text:
{
  "entry_id": "room_temperature_hold_band",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The air conditioning holds this laboratory's room temperature to roughly plus or minus one degree.",
  "numbers": [
    {
      "name": "temperature_stability",
      "value": 1,
      "unit": "K",
      "at": "ambient",
      "source": "operator_recall:kyuhwan_20260923",
      "grade": "E5",
      "precision": "order_of_magnitude",
      "note": "The half-width of the band, as the operator gave it: 'about plus or minus one degree'. Filed at order_of_magnitude because the answer carried its own hedge -- it says the band is of order one kelvin, not that it is one kelvin rather than a half or two."
    }
  ],
  "validity_conditions": "THE ROOM, NOT THE SAMPLE, and as recalled rather than logged. room_temperature_is_controlled records that the room is held continuously and names three things it does not know: the setpoint, how tightly the room holds it, and how well the sample follows the room. This entry answers the second, at the recollection grade. The first -- the setpoint -- is not recorded here; the one reading the store has is lab_ambient_temperature's 20 degC, which is a reading and not the setpoint. The third is still open and is the one that matters for anything at the sample: illumination, a contacting objective, the stage and the trapping laser each move the sample independently of the room (no_thermometer_at_the_sample, trap_heating_detection_bound). SO A ROOM VALUE APPLIED TO THE SAMPLE STANDS ON THAT GAP, NOT ON THIS ENTRY. WHAT IT DOES FOR A CALLER: combined with room_thermometer_reads_in_one_kelvin_steps, a card taking the room reading as a condition has two graded reasons to ask over an interval of a kelvin or two rather than at a point. In explore mode that interval moves nothing that matters -- water's viscosity changes by about two percent per kelvin and its density by about two parts in ten thousand -- and in confirm mode it is exactly what has to be carried. ANSWERS A NAME ALREADY ASKED: temperature_stability was asked by the microscope question's a5 on 2026-09-19 and came back absent.",
  "subject": [
    { "kind": "quantity", "id": "temperature_stability" },
    { "kind": "quantity", "id": "ambient_temperature" },
    { "kind": "quantity", "id": "temperature" }
  ],

  "grade": "E5",
  "grade_tag": "operator_recall",
  "source_ref": "src_operator_recall_20260923",
  "valid_until": {
    "event": "the air conditioning or its control is changed, or a logged record of the room temperature over time is taken, which would supersede this with a measured band."
  },
  "date": "2026-09-23",

}

room_temperature_is_controlled.text:
{
  "entry_id": "room_temperature_is_controlled",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The room is held continuously by air conditioning. There is a setpoint on this instrument's environment -- it is the room's, not the sample's.",
  "subject": [
    { "kind": "quantity", "id": "temperature" },
    { "kind": "quantity", "id": "ambient_temperature" }
  ],
  "source": "operator_read:kyuhwan_20260919",
  "grade": "E3",
  "grade_tag": "operator_read",
  "source_ref": "src_operator_read_20260919",
  "validity_conditions": "This laboratory as of 2026-09-19, read by the operator. It runs opposite to how it sounds, and that is the reason it is worth an entry: holding the room does not shrink the sample question, it ISOLATES it. With the room held, whatever still moves at the sample is local -- illumination, a contacting objective, the stage, the trapping laser -- and each of those has its own gap. Do not read 'the room is controlled' as 'temperature is handled'. That grade never rested on the argument and did not move; the reasoning did. What this entry does NOT say: what the setpoint is, how tightly the room holds it, and how well the sample follows the room. {
  "entry_id": "tau_d",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "derived_quantity",
  "claim": "The diffusive time is the time a sphere needs to diffuse its own diameter, and it sets the shortest record length from which a mean squared displacement can be read.",
  "symbol": "tau_d",
  "formula": "bead_diameter**2/diffusivity",
  "inputs": [
    "bead_diameter",
    "diffusivity"
  ],
  "unit": "s",
  "validity_conditions": "A length squared over a diffusivity is a TIME, and the unit above says so: this is a derived quantity that keeps a dimension, not a dimensionless group. Physically: spherical tracer, bulk fluid, no slip, overdamped. Near a wall the drag is corrected separately rather than absorbed into this time, or the time unit changes with stage position and nothing can be compared. ITS INPUTS ARE FORMAL PARAMETERS, AND THAT IS THE COMPLETE AND PERMANENT STATE. `bead_diameter` and `diffusivity` name the ARGUMENTS of a relation, not particular values in this store, and check 62 correctly reports that nothing carries them. That is not a gap waiting on a later milestone -- 4.3.1 separates looked-for-and-absent from there-is-nothing-to-look-for, and this is the second. Binding them to entries would be worse than leaving them: pointing `bead_diameter` at tracer_diameter_measured would make a relation true of ANY sphere read as a claim about one bottle on one bench, which is the instance/type error with the subject changed. AND A FORMULA HAS NO WORST INPUT TO INHERIT. 5.3's max(E4, worst input) is a rule about a computed VALUE, where the inputs are numbers carrying grades. A relation composes no numbers, so there is no worst input -- not one the store is missing, one the object does not have. This entry is E4 because the relation is textbook, which is what grade_tag and src_colloid_dynamics say, and it would still be E4 in a store holding no diameters at all. Ruled 2026-09-20 under task 020: a derived_quantity whose inputs are formal parameters is a COMPLETE entry and belongs on no fix list. Nothing check 62 reads was changed to make it say so.",

    {
      "kind": "quantity",
      "id": "tau_d"
    }
  ],
  "grade": "E4",

tracer_diameter_measured.text:
{
  "entry_id": "tracer_diameter_measured",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "calibration",
  "claim": "The particles in the bottle in use have a diameter of 5 micrometres, with a coefficient of variation no greater than 2 per cent, measured directly by the operator on 2026-09-19.",
  "numbers": [
    {
      "name": "tracer_diameter",
      "value": 5,
      "unit": "um",
      "source": "calibration:tracer_diameter_20260919",
      "grade": "E2",
      "precision": "significant_figures"
    },
    {
      "name": "tracer_diameter_cv_upper_bound",
      "value": 0.02,
      "unit": "1",
      "source": "calibration:tracer_diameter_20260919",
      "grade": "E2",
      "precision": "significant_figures",
      "note": "A FRACTION, AND IT READS CORRECTLY WITHOUT THIS NOTE -- 0.02 dimensionless is the whole claim. It was `value: 2, unit: \"1\"` for a day, which evaluates to 200 per cent, with the per-cent carried in prose right here because the registry had no unit for it. The reasoning was honest and it put the fact where nothing computes: a distinction living only in a note is one a query cannot act on, which is the shape this store spent two days removing from elsewhere before reproducing it here (019). AN UPPER BOUND, NOT A POINT VALUE -- the person said within 2 per cent, not 2 per cent, so 0.02 is a ceiling on the spread and not its size. REGISTERING A `percent` UNIT WAS OFFERED AND DECLINED. It is multiplicative and would survive the registry's operations, unlike degC, so the offer was sound; what it costs is a second dimensionless spelling beside `1`, which puts a conversion in the path of every query comparing dimensionless quantities, for the readability of one number. The store fixed `dimensionless` versus `1` yesterday and that was a true synonym while this would not be -- but the cost lands on consumers either way. If CVs become common the trade flips and this should be revisited. WHAT THE SPREAD IS OF is not recorded -- how many particles, sized how -- and is a gap."
    }
  ],
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "sample",
      "id": "particle_suspension_a"
    }
  ],
  "source": "calibration:tracer_diameter_20260919",
  "grade": "E2",
  "grade_tag": "calibration",
  "source_ref": "src_cal_tracer_diameter_20260919",
  "valid_until": {
    "date": "2036-09-19",
    "event": "a different bottle of particles is put into use, or this one is re-suspended from a different stock. The event is the real condition and the date is only an outer bound: this measurement is about the contents of one bottle, so what ends it is the bottle ending, not time passing"
  },
  "validity_conditions": "THE SCOPE IS AN INSTANCE, AND IT LIVES IN `subject`, NOT IN `validity`. This entry was blocked for part of 2026-09-19 because a `calibration:` source required a machine-readable `validity`, and a condition_range is quantity-to-interval while what bounds this measurement is a bottle. manager-librarian ruled the right answer, which was none of the three options raised: an instance is a SUBJECT, not a condition. What stops this being applied to another bottle is the subject, and `validity` exists for the case the pixel-size calibrations have, where a claim holds only at 1x1 binning. `valid_until` stayed unconditionally required, because it carries the event, and `an unbounded calibration is a measurement with no event` was the load-bearing half of that rule. IT DOES NOT RUN THROUGH THE IDENTIFICATION, AND THAT IS THE POINT. A measurement made on the bottle does not pass through `identified_as` in the sample table and does not inherit its E5. The 5 um that stood on the product name was type-level and weak; this 5 um is instance-level and E2. Same number, entirely different standing. If the bottle turns out to be another product, this stays true of the bottle and only the type-level facts move. IT OUTRANKS THE LOT. E2 is above the E3 a `spec:<lot>` would have given, so the lot number this gap had been waiting on is not needed for the diameter. The lot narrows rather than vanishing: the prior project recorded that size CV and dye loading both vary lot to lot, and size CV is now measured and out of the lot's hands, leaving dye loading -- tracer_brightness, still unmeasured, still lot-dependent, and read by A1. IT SETTLES A STANDING DISAGREEMENT. The simulation's `assumed:` 2 um and the microscope's `operator_recall:` 5 um were both E5 with neither outranking the other, which is what opened 11-13. One side is now a measurement, so the argument goes from `a weak claim beats a blank` to `a measurement beats a blank`. THE CV IS AN UPPER BOUND AND IT BUYS SOMETHING DOWNSTREAM. Within 2 per cent makes the spread in diffusivity across particles about 4 per cent, since D goes as 1/d, which is inside explore's tie band. Worth stating because nobody was accounting for polydispersity and nothing on disk said why that was safe. WHAT IS NOT RECORDED: how it was measured.   "entry_id": "tracer_diffusivity_expected",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "derived_quantity",
  "claim": "The expected translational diffusivity of a tracer sphere in a bulk fluid is the Stokes-Einstein value, k_B T over 3 pi eta d. It is a prediction from the viscosity, the temperature and the diameter, not a measurement of how the particles actually move.",
  "symbol": "tracer_diffusivity_expected",
  "formula": "k_B*ambient_temperature/(3*pi*viscosity*tracer_diameter)",
  "inputs": [
    "ambient_temperature",
    "viscosity",
    "tracer_diameter"
  ],
  "unit": "um^2/s",
  "source": "computed:stokes_einstein",
  "grade": "E4",
  "grade_tag": "textbook",
  "source_ref": "src_colloid_dynamics",
  "validity_conditions": "A SPHERE IN BULK, WHICH IS WHERE THIS STOPS BEING TRUE FIRST. Stokes-Einstein assumes a rigid sphere, no slip at its surface, a continuum Newtonian fluid, dilute suspension so particles do not feel each other, and low Reynolds number. Near a wall the drag rises and the real diffusivity falls below this value -- the correction is applied separately and is NOT absorbed here, for the reason tau_d gives: fold it in and the quantity changes with stage position and nothing can be compared across runs. A tracer sitting on a coverslip is the case where this entry is most likely to be quietly wrong.\n\nWHY AN ENTRY RATHER THAN EACH CARD COMPUTING IT. plan.md:1295 ruled it: recomputing a quantity the store holds is not estimation, it is a detour. A simulation card cast tau_a = radius**2/D at E5 while kb:tau_d held diameter**2/D at E4 -- a factor of four out and a grade worse. A card citing this gets one name and the better grade; a card computing it gets neither. Filed as a formula rather than a value so that when an input improves the entry improves with it: the diameter went from an E5 recollection to an E2 measurement on 2026-09-19 and nothing here needs rewriting for that.\n\nTHE GRADE IS E4 AND THE CHECK DOES NOT DERIVE IT. 5.3 makes a `computed:` source max(E4, worst input). The worst input is E3 -- water_viscosity_293k E3, lab_ambient_temperature E3, tracer_diameter_measured E2 -- so E4. Check 43 does NOT confirm this: its `computed:` branch accepts E4 or E5 and never reads the inputs, so the number above is a reading of 5.3 by two people and not something the run established. Said out loud because 019 asked for the grade as the validator derives it, and the validator derives a range.\n\nTHE TEMPERATURE IS THE ROOM'S, NOT THE SAMPLE'S, AND THAT IS AN ASSUMPTION THIS ENTRY CARRIES. lab_ambient_temperature is a thermometer reading of the room; nothing actuates or reads the sample temperature (no_thermometer_at_the_sample, sample_temperature_not_actuated). declared_versus_inferred_temperature records why this is not symmetric between the two agents: the simulation DECLARES its temperature and realises it, so citing one there records a choice; the experiment INFERS it, so citing one there is a claim about the sample. This entry is on the inferring side. Under a trapping laser it is worse -- trap_heating_detection_bound bounds the heating only below about 20 per cent of the IR power and says nothing above it.\n\nUNITS: THE FORMULA IS SI AND THE DECLARED UNIT IS NOT. Evaluate with k_B in J/K, the temperature in K, the viscosity in Pa*s and the diameter in METRES, and the result is m^2/s. The entry declares um^2/s because that is the scale this store and both agents report diffusivity in -- quantities.json records the whole family at um^2/s -- and units.json's si_factor is what converts. Putting the diameter in um while the viscosity is in Pa*s and reading the answer as um^2/s is out by a factor of 10^6, which is six orders and would not look like a slip in a log.\n\nNOT `tracer_diffusivity`, AND NOT `diffusivity`. Three near-names now sit in one family and two of them are already in quantities.json's open_collisions. `tracer_diffusivity` is the REGISTERED OBSERVABLE: what an experiment measures and what the bridge threads between the two agents. `diffusivity` is the name the simulation writes, six uses, colliding with that observable. This one is the PREDICTION -- what Stokes-Einstein says the value should be given the inputs. The distinction is load-bearing rather than pedantic: the whole point of thr-tracer-diffusivity-001 is to compare a measured diffusivity against a modelled one, and an expected value quietly substituted for either side would make the comparison compare a prediction with itself. `_expected` is the word that keeps them apart and it has to survive any later rename.\n\nNO `subject`, AND THE REASON CHANGED ON 2026-09-20 WHILE THE ANSWER DID NOT. What this paragraph said until now: a quantity subject must resolve against check 44's registry -- the names used in numbers[] anywhere, united with those declared in contracts/quantities.json -- and `tracer_diffusivity_expected` was in neither, because this entry is a formula carrying no numbers[] and the two microscope axes that want it name it in `missing[]` and in a gap's `observable`, which the registry does not read. That was a BLOCK and it named manager-librarian as the route out. THE BLOCK IS GONE: the id is now declared in contracts/quantities.json, measured there on 2026-09-20 among sixteen, so a quantity subject would resolve today. Left off anyway, and now for a standing reason rather than a blocked one: `Store.subjects` is a UNION over entry_id, symbol, numbers[].name, subject[].id and the addressable identifiers, and both entry_id and symbol are already this exact string -- so a subject naming it would add no handle that is not already there. Measured and not reasoned: `answers_to` returns this entry for the bare name today, with the field absent. It stays empty because it would be a duplicate, not because anything is waiting on anybody. WRITTEN OUT RATHER THAN DELETED: a sentence saying a landed thing is still owed sends the next reader to raise it a second time, which is the failure this repository keeps recording, and deleting it instead would leave that reader to rediscover that a quantity subject is possible here and wonder why nobody filled it.\n\nITS INPUTS ARE FORMAL PARAMETERS TOO, AND FOR A WHILE THAT WAS HIDDEN BY A COINCIDENCE. Task 020 ruled that a derived_quantity whose inputs are formal parameters is complete and takes no grade from them -- 5.3's max(E4, worst input) is a rule about a computed VALUE, and a relation composes no numbers. That ruling was argued about tau_d and it applies here identically: this is the same kind, with the same `formula` key, and `ambient_temperature`, `viscosity` and `tracer_diameter` are the arguments of Stokes-Einstein, not references to particular entries. What made check 62 treat the two differently was that these three names HAPPEN to be carried as values in this store while tau_d's `bead_diameter` is the open_collisions synonym of `tracer_diameter` and is carried by nothing. So the grade it derived here was a coincidence of vocabulary, and editing one string inside the formula would have created or destroyed it -- which is option 2 of task 020, refused at the front door, arriving at the side. manager-librarian caught this in the seat that wrote the ruling and reported the derived count as 2. This entry's E4 comes from the relation being textbook and would stand in a store holding no diameters at all.",

}

What crossed is the finding about the vendor's published data, which is about Abvigen and attaches to no bottle at all. Found by librarian-agent-a5 verifying my report against the tree, which is exactly why that verification was handed over: my account came from memory of what I had done. The entry_id still begins `tracer_` and stays that way deliberately -- it is the citation handle, the polystyrene dispersion entries reference it by name, and renaming it is a deletion under rule 8. `conflict_with` IS NOW EMPTY AND `refuted_by` CARRIES IT, AND THE REASON MATTERS BECAUSE IT LOOKS LIKE A RULE 7 VIOLATION AND IS NOT. Rule 7 says conflicts are kept and both sides marked, never merged. Nothing is merged here and nothing is deleted -- this entry stays, at its grade, with its number. Both directions are written, `refuted_by` here and `refutes` on the observation, so a caller arriving from either end sees it.",

}

trap_heating_detection_bound.text:
{
  "entry_id": "trap_heating_detection_bound",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The operator recalls not noticing a temperature change in the sample unless the infrared trapping laser was driven above roughly 20 percent on its dial. This records where noticing stopped, by means that were not recorded.",
  "subject": [
    { "kind": "device", "id": "optical_tweezers" },
    { "kind": "configuration", "id": "trapping" },
    { "kind": "quantity", "id": "temperature" }
  ],
  "source": "operator_recall:kyuhwan_20260919",
  "grade": "E5",
  "grade_tag": "operator_recall",
  "source_ref": "src_operator_recall_20260919",
  "validity_conditions": "THIS IS NOT A LIMIT AND MAY NOT BE USED AS ONE. 'Keep it under 20 percent' is the sentence someone lifts out of an entry and uses to parameterise a laser, and three separate rules forbid that: safety limits live in a file a person writes and in deterministic code (P0, 2.1 rule 7), they do not transfer (10.3 rule 4), and the grade forbids it on its own -- an E5 may not parameterise an irreversible action without a person's individual approval, and raising laser power onto a sample is irreversible to the sample. Anyone needing a bound writes one in envelope/safety.json after confirming it physically. Three things this says less than it appears to. It is RECALLED, not read, which is why it is E5 while the neighbouring instrument facts are E3. It is a DETECTION BOUND and not a zero: 'did not notice' was measured by unrecorded means, and 'no heating below 20 percent' is a stronger claim than was made. And 20 PERCENT IS A DIAL READING, not a power: a percentage of an unstated maximum is not a quantity, and writing it into numbers[] would not make it one -- the same ruling that keeps a nominal magnification out of numbers[], wearing different clothes. It does not close the heating gap. A measured heating rate is still absent, and a gap that looks satisfied by an E5 recollection is a false absence running backwards. What it does is sharpen what to measure: sweep the dial with a thermometer that has a recorded position, and the bound becomes a curve.",
  "date": "2026-09-19",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

  "claim": "The optical tweezers' trapping laser can be switched on and off from software: the Tweez 300 TCP/IP command set includes LASER_ON (activates the laser) and LASER_OFF (deactivates it). The command set holds no command that sets or reads the laser's power.",
