  "validity_conditions": "The Tweez 300 as installed on this bench, driven through its TCP/IP external control. Read from the User Manual's Command Reference, printed page 66 (PDF page 72); the whole command list was searched for a power, intensity or laser command and only these two exist. The manual's Laser Control section (printed page 23) adds that the laser activates only if every laser safety component is connected and every interlock is enabled -- stated for the GUI button, and the Command Reference says each command is an exact counterpart of the GUI procedure.\n\nWHY THIS IS HERE. trap_laser_power_has_no_software_path is right about POWER and says nothing about EMISSION, and its name reads as if software has no way to reach the laser at all. It does: software cannot set the level, and it can turn emission on. That is the more dangerous half to leave out, and microscope-20260924-4 reported it on 2026-09-24. Neither command has been sent on this bench; this is the vendor's documentation, not an observation.\n\nNOT A POLICY. Whether any session may send LASER_ON is a person's decision and lives in the envelope, not here.",

  "validity_conditions": "Ruled TRANSFER under 10.2.1 and passed 10.3 rule 1, so it caps at E3 -- a run taken in another project is not a run taken here. 10.2's hardware-control-path row is open and says in its own rule that it does not wait for envelope/, because wrapping a control path needs no safety limit. The power a sample sees is a separate fact and it is absent (gap trap_power_at_the_sample). A RATED MAXIMUM IS NOT A PERMISSION. 5 W is what the device can emit, not what this laboratory allows; what it allows is written by a person in envelope/safety.json, and that file does not exist. 10.2 gates transferred spec values on exactly that file, with the reason that a spec number not placed beside limit values gets used as a limit -- the gate applies to transfers and so does not block this entry, which came from the operator, but the hazard it names does not care where the number came from. NOT MACHINE-READABLE, and that is a limit of the schema rather than of this entry: `validity` carries quantity-to-interval pairs, so 'at the generator' has nowhere to go and a query cannot act on it. This is the second such case -- the first being that lab_ambient_temperature is a reading of the room and not of the sample -- and both are raised with manager-librarian. tweez300_reports_nothing_back.text:
{
  "entry_id": "tweez300_reports_nothing_back",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The Tweez 300's TCP interface has no readback of any kind -- no position, no force, no trap list, no calibration -- and a return code of 0 means the GUI accepted the command, not that anything happened. Six distinct ways a command can be ignored all return 0: a breakpoint whose enable bits are unset, release bits that do not cover the value, repeat left disabled, a pattern that overruns the calibrated range and is silently clipped to the edge, a GUI calibrated at a different objective so every commanded micrometre is wrong by that ratio, and a named trap that holds no bead.",
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "device",
      "id": "optical_tweezers"
    },
    {
      "kind": "configuration",
      "id": "trapping"
    }
  ],
  "source": "prior_run:agentic-microscope@safety-2026-09-03",
  "grade": "E3",
  "source_ref": "src_prior_safety_memo",
  "validity_conditions": "Ruled TRANSFER under 10.2.1 and passed 10.3 rule 1, so it caps at E3 -- a run taken in another project is not a run taken here. 10.2's hardware-control-path row is open and says in its own rule that it does not wait for envelope/, because wrapping a control path needs no safety limit. Slot: A4, which screens on automatable and read_back, with O1 preflight as the second consumer -- a preflight that reads back to confirm has nothing to read here. This is what read_back: false means on that row, stated rather than left as a flag. Confirmation has to come from outside the interface: by eye in the GUI, or by measuring the result in camera data. Note the contrast with the piezo, which range-checks a trajectory against the travel its controller reports and REFUSES rather than clipping -- two devices on one instrument, opposite behaviours at the same boundary, and only one of them tells you.",
  "date": "2026-09-19",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

working_distance_is_measured_to_the_cove.text:
{
  "entry_id": "working_distance_is_measured_to_the_coverslip",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The catalogue working distances for the objectives on this nosepiece are measured from the front element to the coverslip's lens-facing surface, not to the sample plane. This is inferred from two facts the store already holds; no document was read that says it.",
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "device",
      "id": "nosepiece"
    }
  ],
  "inputs": ["working_distance", "coverslip_thickness"],
  "source": "computed:working_distance_versus_coverslip",
  "grade": "E4",
  "grade_tag": "computed",
  "source_ref": "src_store_derivation",
  "validity_conditions": "THE INFERENCE, AND IT IS AN INFERENCE. Three of the six objectives have a catalogue working distance SHORTER than the coverslip this laboratory mounts on: 60x Oil at 150 um (objective_mrd71670), 100x Oil at 130 um (objective_mrd71970), and 40x WI from 160 um (objective_mrd77400), against coverslip_thickness 170 um (coverslip_thickness_in_use, E3, operator_read). If the catalogue measured to the SAMPLE PLANE, then at focus the front element of those three would sit nearer the sample than the glass is thick -- inside the coverslip. It cannot. So the catalogue measures to the coverslip's lens-facing surface, and the distance from front element to sample is the working distance plus the coverslip thickness.\n\nRECORDED AS AN INFERENCE OR NOT AT ALL, which is how task 021 put it and why this is E4 rather than E3. Nothing was read. Two E3 facts and one impossibility give it, and 5.3 caps a consequence at E4 however good its inputs are. A later reading of the Nikon catalogue that states the convention outright would supersede this at E3; a measurement on this bench would do better still.\n\nWHAT IT IS NOT NEEDED FOR. Not for the focus ceiling. Task 021 recorded the person's correction of an over-built argument: a lens is at its working distance when it is in focus, by definition, so `do not pass the working distance` means `do not pass focus` whichever surface the catalogue measured from. The convention does not enter that rule and the ceiling did not wait on it.\n\nWHAT IT IS NEEDED FOR. Anything computing an absolute Z in stage coordinates from the coverslip geometry -- where the sample plane sits relative to a focused objective, how far a stage may travel before the element meets glass, and any conversion between a focus position and a depth in the sample. Those need the plus-170 and get it wrong silently without this.\n\nWHY THIS ONE DERIVES AND declared_versus_inferred_temperature DOES NOT. Both are conclusions this store reasoned to rather than read, and both are `computed:` at E4. The difference is what they rest on: this rests on two QUANTITIES the store carries as numbers, `working_distance` and `coverslip_thickness`, so `inputs` resolves and check 62 can verify the grade. That entry rests on CLAIMS carrying no numbers, so nothing composes. Same source kind, two different shapes -- which is the gap raised with manager-librarian under task 020.",
  "date": "2026-09-20",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

  "validity_conditions": "Ruled TRANSFER under 10.2.1 and passed 10.3 rule 1, so it caps at E3 -- a run taken in another project is not a run taken here. 10.2's hardware-control-path row is open and says in its own rule that it does not wait for envelope/, because wrapping a control path needs no safety limit. Slot: O1 preflight and the orchestrator, both of which move Z. It carries no number and no limit -- a direction is not a permission. It is transferred BECAUSE it replaced a guess that ran the other way: the earlier reading had been that larger Z was retracted, taken from the fact that one rotation at a high Z broke nothing, and under the measured convention that rotation drove the incoming lens millimetres PAST the sample plane, so nothing broke because nothing was in the way. Anyone following the old guess would have driven the objective toward the coverslip believing they were retracting. The source document's own open-questions list still says this direction is unmeasured and calls it the most consequential gap in the document; the body of the same document records the measurement two days later. The list is stale, not the measurement -- see the pfs_offset_sign_unmeasured gap for the direction that really is still open.",
  "date": "2026-09-19",

}

samples.text:
{
  "schema_version": "0.1-provisional",
  "kind": "sample_instances",
  "storage_form": "PROVISIONAL, and a flat table for the same reason devices.v0.json is one. Unlike that file this was not extracted from anywhere: it is new, created 2026-09-19 because task 016 established that the store had no way to name the thing on the bench.",
  "created_at": "2026-09-19",
  "why_this_file_exists": "Found by refusing to game check 44. The bead entries could carry no `subject` because there is no registry a sample resolves against, and the fields were removed rather than filled with an id that would make them pass. Task 015 then showed where the claim had gone instead -- into the entry NAMES, `tracer_particle_density`, where nothing checks it. A check rejecting the honest form of an assertion is what proved the registry was needed.",
  "the_ruling_this_implements": "Architecture, 6eaee1b. THE INSTANCE/TYPE SPLIT IS THE WHOLE RULING. A measurement is made on an INSTANCE; a specification is written about a TYPE; and the claim joining them carries its own grade. If the bottle turns out to be another product, an observation made on it stays true of the bottle and becomes false of the product -- which is why the first column cannot be a catalogue number. Putting all three in one cell is what happened to the pixel size earlier the same day: grading a value before settling what it is about.",
  "why_not_inside_the_device_table": "Every column there is false of a sample: `driver`, `automatable`, `read_back`, `lock_group`. Same argument that kept the room thermometer out of it.",
  "why_not_the_microscope_run_records": "Two reasons from architecture. One sample is used by TWO agents -- the simulation models it as well -- and a bottle outlives a run.",
  "naming_rule": "AN INSTANCE ID MUST NOT ENCODE A PRODUCT. `abvigen_bottle` would bake the very claim that carries its own grade into the identifier, which is the disease this table exists to cure. Ids describe what the thing observably is, plus a letter to tell instances apart.",
  "consumers": {
    "librarian": "resolves `subject` of kind sample for entries about an instance",
    "a1": "tracer brightness and detectability are about the instance in the tub",
    "a6": "the collected wavelength depends on what is actually fluorescing",
    "simulation": "models the same sample and must name the same instance"
  },
  "instances": [
    {
      "id": "particle_suspension_a",
      "what_it_observably_is": "an aqueous suspension of particles in use on the microscope bench, which fluoresce under green excitation and are visible through the 605 band",
      "first_recorded": "2026-09-19",
      "label": {
        "read": true,
        "read_on": "2026-09-19",
        "states_a_product": false,
        "entry_ref": "bottle_label_states_no_product",
        "note": "LOOKED AT AND SILENT, which is different from not checked. This is what makes the identification permanently open rather than pending: the one thing that might have settled it has happened and did not."
      },
      "identified_as": {
        "type": "AFR-0500-COOH",
        "grade": "E5",
        "source": "assumed:person_ruling_20260919",
        "why_e5": "THE JOINING CLAIM CARRIES ITS OWN GRADE AND THIS IS IT. Not `operator_read:` -- nobody read it off the bottle. Not `operator_recall:` -- it is not a memory. It is the person's reasoned judgement from named evidence, which is `assumed:` and E5. EVERY TYPE-LEVEL FACT APPLIED TO THIS BOTTLE INHERITS THIS GRADE by 5.8, worst in the chain. So the material, the density, the 5 um diameter and the number-density relation reach this instance at E5, not at the E3 they carry about the type.",
        "evidence_for": [
          "abvigen_published_data_is_unreliable -- the supplier's page carries errors unrelated to spectra, so `the data sheet is wrong` is a cheaper explanation than `the bottle is not the product`",
          "the prior project tested the same catalogue product and found the same disagreement with the published spectra, independently"
        ],
        "evidence_against": [
          "the label says nothing, so nothing positively identifies this bottle"
        ],
        "what_would_settle_it": "a label, an invoice, or a lot number that names the product. Any of them moves this to `spec:<lot>` at E3 and lifts every type-level fact with it.",
        "history": "Task 015 ruled on 2026-09-19 that the product was the WRONG one, and the person reversed it the same day once the prior project's records were opened. Recorded rather than erased: 015's evidence was a silent label, which is equally consistent with both explanations, and what actually decided it was the asymmetry in how careless the vendor's page is. Anyone re-deriving this from the label alone will reach 015 again."
      },
      "observed_on_this_instance": [
        {
          "entry_ref": "particles_show_on_the_green_605_path",
          "grade": "E2",
          "what": "fluoresces under Aura3 green, visible through the 605 band"
        },
        {
          "entry_ref": "bottle_label_states_no_product",
          "grade": "E3",
          "what": "the label states no product identity"
        },
        {
          "entry_ref": "tracer_diameter_measured",
          "grade": "E2",
          "what": "diameter 5 um, CV within 2 per cent, measured directly"
        }
      ],
      "type_facts_reach_this_instance_via": "identified_as, at E5",
      "what_now_points_here": "Three entries carry `subject: [{kind: sample, id: particle_suspension_a}]` as of a675c4e, which added `sample` to the subject enum and wired check 44 to resolve it against THIS FILE and nothing else. That wiring matters: the `quantity` kind resolves against names used in numbers[] anywhere, which an entry can satisfy by itself -- and on 2026-09-19 renaming one number dangled five subjects that had only ever resolved against a number in the same file. A registry an entry can write itself into is not a registry. Verified: querying `particle_suspension_a` returns all three."
    }
  ],
  "types_referenced": {
    "why": "NOT A PRODUCT TABLE. Architecture ruled this file names instances, and it does. This section exists only so `identified_as.type` resolves against something instead of being a free string -- which is precisely the failure that produced 015, a claim asserted in text nothing checks. It lists the designations instances point at and holds no facts about them; the facts are ordinary entries at E3.",
    "AFR-0500-COOH": {
      "supplier": "Abvigen Inc",
      "entries": [
        "tracer_particle_material_and_shape",
        "tracer_particle_density",
        "tracer_stock_concentration",
        "tracer_storage_conditions",
        "tracer_number_density_from_diameter",
        "tracer_emission_peak",
        "tracer_excitation_peak"
      ],
      "caution": "abvigen_published_data_is_unreliable applies to every one of these. Two of them, the excitation and emission peaks, are marked DISPROVED by two independent instrument observations and are kept only under rule 8."
    }
  },
  "gaps": [
    {
      "what": "the lot number",
      "kind": "absent",
      "searched": [
        "the bottle label"
      ],
      "status": "The prior project's record also has `lot: null -- not on the product page, read it off the tube`. Nobody has. This is the cheapest thing on the list that would lift the joining claim to E3.",
      "why_it_matters": "it is the identifier a person can verify by looking, which 10.2 names as the one thing worth carrying about a consumable"
    },
    {
      "what": "the dilution between the stock bottle and the coverslip",
      "kind": "absent",
      "searched": [
        "kb/entries",
        "the microscope agent's run records"
      ],
      "status": "Recorded nowhere, and no card has asked for it. So even with a diameter, the number density under the objective does not follow from the stock concentration -- there is an unrecorded factor in between.",
      "why_it_matters": "tracer_number_density in any real sample"
    }
  ],
  "a_correction_recorded_in_place": "THIS FILE SAID THE DIAMETER `DOES NOT RESOLVE AND GOT WORSE`, AND THAT WAS ALREADY FALSE WHEN WRITTEN. The measurement landed at 19:41; this table was written after it and did not know. It is the exact failure librarian_agent/CLAUDE.md describes -- a reference that was correct when taken and wrong when used -- committed by the seat that had spent the day counting it in others. Recorded here rather than silently overwritten, because the file is young enough that the diff would otherwise be the only trace.",
  "resolved_gaps": [
    {
      "what": "the particle diameter",
      "searched": [
        "the bottle label",
        "kb/entries",
        "the prior project's records"
      ],
      "status": "CLOSED. Measured by the person on 2026-09-19 -- 5 um, CV within 2 per cent -- and now in the store as tracer_diameter_measured, `calibration:tracer_diameter_20260919` at E2. That is above the E3 a `spec:<lot>` would have given, so the lot is not needed for the diameter: the question this gap put to a person was answered by measurement, and answered better than it was asked. The entry was blocked for part of the day because a `calibration:` source required a machine-readable `validity` and an instance has no interval shape; manager-librarian ruled that an instance is a SUBJECT rather than a condition, and the entry carries `subject: [{kind: sample, id: particle_suspension_a}]` instead.",
      "why_it_matters": "tracer_diffusivity and the number-density relation both stand on it",
      "why_this_one_does_not_hang_off_the_link": "AND THIS IS THE INSTANCE/TYPE SPLIT PAYING FOR ITSELF ON ITS FIRST DAY. A measurement made on the bottle does NOT run through `identified_as` and does NOT inherit its E5. The 5 um that stood on the product name was type-level and weak; the 5 um that was measured is instance-level and E2. Same number, and everything about its standing is different. If the bottle later turns out to be another product, this measurement stays true of the bottle.",
      "what_the_lot_still_owes": "The lot narrows rather than vanishing. The prior project recorded that size CV and dye loading both vary lot to lot; size CV is now measured directly and out of the lot's hands, leaving dye loading -- which is tracer_brightness, still unmeasured, still lot-dependent, and read by A1.",
      "the_disagreement_it_settles": "The simulation's `assumed:` 2 um and the microscope's `operator_recall:` 5 um were symmetric at E5 with neither outranking the other. One side is now a measurement. The argument goes from `a weak claim beats a blank` to `a measurement beats a blank`.",
      "polydispersity": "CV within 2 per cent is an upper bound, dimensionless, and it makes the spread in diffusivity across particles about 4 per cent since D goes as 1/d -- inside explore's tie band. Worth recording because nobody was accounting for polydispersity and nothing said why that was safe.",
      "entry_ref": "tracer_diameter_measured"
    }
  ],
  "why_resolved_gaps_is_separate": "Following devices.v0.json, which keeps `gaps` and `resolved_gaps` apart. The diameter sat in `gaps` with a status of CLOSED for a few minutes, which mixed two states in one list, and it carried `kind: absent_from_this_store_only` -- a FIFTH spelling of a field whose four values exist precisely because the next action differs. A table a caller reads directly is the worst place to invent a fifth. librarian-agent-a5 caught both."
}

handles.note: every name kb_query and kb_get answer to at this kb_version, with where each comes from. Matching folds case and nothing else, so a name not here does not answer -- there are no synonyms, and asking for one gets `absent` even when the store holds the fact under another word.

how_to_verify: sha256 of each entry's `text` must equal its `sha256`, and sha256 over the canonical JSON of this object without `snapshot_hash` must equal `snapshot_hash`. A hand-edited copy fails both. `built_from_commit` names the commit this was built from, so every byte here is readable back with `git show <commit>:<path>` -- a kb_version identifies the knowledge and this identifies the packaging. Do not edit a copy: fix the KB and re-export (4.3.2).
